- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.30) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.30), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for potential reversal.  
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), leading to overshoot; cap forecast peak at 10–15% above recent high.  
- If 3–5 consecutive days show mean reversion (price falling after rising), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% lag correction to forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates long-term trend; apply 1–3% upward bias if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.30 → -0.40 → +0.20), model misreads momentum; use sentiment-weighted moving average for smoothing.
